target.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens
target.body:
Closes #98107

## Summary

- Preserve existing generated macOS LaunchAgent env-file values for config SecretRef environment keys when the install plan regenerates the gateway service environment.
- Pass installed service environment value-source metadata through start-time stale-service repair, so repair-on-start uses the same preservation path as install/reinstall.
- Track current config SecretRef env ids as managed service keys even when the current shell no longer contains the secret value.
- Keep fresh state-dir `.env` and current shell SecretRef values ahead of older generated env-file values.
- Rebased the PR onto current `origin/main` and resolved the service-env planning conflict by retaining main's SecretRef discovery short-circuit while keeping this PR's managed-key tracking.

## What Problem This Solves

Users running the gateway as a macOS LaunchAgent could lose Telegram bot token environment values after service regeneration. The reported failure path is an install/update/restart flow where the initial service env file contained `TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN`, but a later regeneration ran without that env var in the invoking shell and rewrote the generated service-env file without the token.

## User Impact

A configured Telegram channel can fail after gateway restart or update because the LaunchAgent restarts with an env file that no longer contains the bot token. Preserving the generated file-backed SecretRef value keeps the channel online while still allowing newer state-dir `.env` or current-shell values to override stale file values.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** A user can complete gateway install with a working Telegram bot, then lose that channel after an update or restart because the regenerated LaunchAgent env file no longer carries the token. The fix protects the user-visible channel availability path without requiring users to re-export secrets before every service regeneration.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root-cause fix for linked bug #98107.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Linked issue: #98107 remains the canonical open bug for the macOS LaunchAgent service-env Telegram token wipe.
- Competition scan / related open PR scan: #96065 added adjacent config SecretRef managed-env tracking, but it did not cover preserving existing generated LaunchAgent env-file values during this restart/update regeneration path.
- This update keeps the existing PR #99124 branch and does not create a replacement PR.

## Scope and source of truth

- **What did NOT change:** This patch is limited to gateway service-env planning/render policy and the start-repair caller path. It does not change Telegram startup, SecretRef syntax, config loading, token generation, non-macOS service behavior, or unrelated extension code; those areas remain out of scope and unchanged.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth contract for whether a reused value may be preserved is the service command environment value-source metadata read from the installed service definition. Only values with generated env-file provenance (`file` / `inline-and-file`) are eligible for preservation, and only while current config still references the normalized SecretRef key as a managed service-env key.
- **Related PR scan:** #96065 was checked as adjacent merged work and does not cover this generated LaunchAgent env-file preservation path; this PR remains the focused fix for #98107.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** macOS LaunchAgent gateway service-env regeneration keeps a Telegram bot token that came from an existing generated env file when the current invocation no longer has `TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN` set.
- **Real environment tested:** zhangguiping-xydt supplied live macOS LaunchAgent proof in the PR discussion for pre-sync head `e4e5ad36fe7c841e2660e9ebafcaa45ba9a5ae70`: temporary LaunchAgent, isolated HOME/state/config, env SecretRef Telegram token, secret-absent update/regeneration, `launchctl print`, and Telegram Bot API `getMe` using the token read back from the regenerated service-env file. After the required `sync-main`, current head `1e554df89789cecdb032a3e030204e0c4fd9ce7c` is the same PR patch series replayed onto current `origin/main`, with one conflict-resolution adaptation that preserves main's `configContainsSecretRef` discovery short-circuit.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** zhangguiping-xydt exercised these live macOS commands on the PR head in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99124#issuecomment-4876537447:

```text
openclaw gateway install --force --json --port <ephemeral> --runtime node
openclaw gateway install --force --json --port <same> --runtime node   # TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN unset
gateway status --deep --json --no-probe
launchctl print gui/<uid>/<temporary-openclaw-proof-label>
Telegram Bot API getMe using the token read from service-env/<label>.env
```

Current synchronized head was validated from the repo root with:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/start-repair.test.ts
pnpm check:no-conflict-markers
pnpm check:test-types
pnpm lint:core
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

- **Evidence after fix:** zhangguiping-xydt reported the live macOS results below, with token and bot identity fields redacted:

```text
Initial install exit code: 0
Update/regeneration with TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN absent exit code: 0
gateway status --deep --json --no-probe after update exit code: 0
Generated service env file before update: existed, mode 0600, token key present, OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS=TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN
Generated service env file after secret-absent update: rewritten, mode 0600, token key still present, managed keys still include TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN
Token equality before/after regeneration: SHA-256 equality check returned true, digest not included
launchctl print: return code 0, state active, pid present, last-exit status empty
Telegram getMe using regenerated env-file token: ok=true, bot id present, username present, can_join_groups=true
Captured CLI stdout/stderr secret scan for raw Telegram token: false
Cleanup: gateway stop/uninstall exit code 0, follow-up launchctl print confirmed the temporary proof label was unloaded
```

Patch continuity after `sync-main`:

```text
1:  18d6aea421 ! 1:  236ecb4b4f Preserve LaunchAgent env-file SecretRefs
    conflict resolution keeps main's configContainsSecretRef short-circuit and this PR's managed-key/environment return shape
2:  dc6dfb228b = 2:  1e554df897 fix gateway start repair env source preservation
```

Current-head local validation:

```text
src/cli/daemon-cli/start-repair.test.ts: 1 test passed
src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts: 48 tests passed
no conflict markers: passed
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD: passed
core test typecheck: passed with no diagnostics
extension test typecheck: passed with no diagnostics
core lint: passed
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The regenerated macOS service env file still contained `TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN` after a secret-absent update, `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MANAGED_ENV_KEYS` still tracked that key, `launchctl print` showed the temporary LaunchAgent active, and Telegram `getMe` succeeded with the token read back from the regenerated file. Current synchronized head also passes the focused regression tests, conflict-marker check, diff check, and test typecheck.
- **What was not tested:** The reported live behavior path was exercised on the pre-sync PR head: macOS LaunchAgent regeneration and Telegram `getMe` both ran in zhangguiping-xydt's proof. The limitation is proof locality after sync: this Linux validation environment validated rebased head `1e554df89789cecdb032a3e030204e0c4fd9ce7c` by patch continuity plus tests/typecheck/static checks, rather than executing macOS `launchctl` again on the rebased SHA.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Maintainer acceptance is still explicitly requested for the macOS LaunchAgent generated-env credential preservation semantics. This update does not hide that as a resolved code defect.
- **RF-002:** The compatibility/security tradeoff remains explicit: older file-backed values are retained only when current config still references the SecretRef key as a managed service-env key, and fresher state-dir `.env` / current shell values still win.
- **RF-003:** The auth/security boundary remains constrained by installed service environment value-source metadata plus current config membership. During conflict resolution, main's `configContainsSecretRef` short-circuit was retained so full target discovery is still skipped for configs without SecretRefs.
- **RF-004:** The branch still has no narrow review defect to repair. This update only resolves the current `origin/main` merge conflict and refreshes current-head verification; remaining acceptance is the documented maintainer judgment on credential-regeneration risk and normal merge gates.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:availability`, `merge-risk:compatibility`, `merge-risk:security-boundary`, `merge-risk:session-state`.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch changes gateway service regeneration behavior for managed env keys that may contain credentials. Availability improves because a running Telegram channel no longer loses its token on LaunchAgent env-file regeneration. Compatibility risk is bounded to macOS LaunchAgent generated env-file preservation; non-macOS rendering and inline-only existing env values are not promoted. Security-boundary risk is bounded by value-source metadata and current config membership, so arbitrary old env values are not copied forward. Session-state risk is bounded because start repair passes through existing metadata instead of inventing new provenance.
- **Why acceptable:** The regenerated env file is already the storage location used by this LaunchAgent install path, and preservation only retains values previously written by the generated env-file path for keys still managed by current config. Newer state-dir `.env` values and current shell SecretRef values still override older generated file values, so the fix does not lock users into stale credentials.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts` covers install-plan preservation and precedence; `src/cli/daemon-cli/start-repair.test.ts` covers the start-repair caller forwarding installed environment value-source metadata.
- **Scenario locked in:** A macOS LaunchAgent install has `TELEGRAM_DEFAULT_BOTTOKEN` in the generated env file with `file` provenance, then the service plan is regenerated while the invoking shell lacks that env var; the regenerated plan must preserve the file-backed token while still letting fresher state-dir `.env` or current shell SecretRef values win.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The helper tests protect the render-policy ordering and managed-key tracking that caused the token wipe, while the start-repair test protects the caller wiring that would otherwise drop `environmentValueSources` before the plan can preserve file-backed values.

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/start-repair.test.ts
pnpm check:no-conflict-markers
pnpm check:test-types
pnpm lint:core
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

```text
All listed commands passed on current synchronized head 1e554df89789cecdb032a3e030204e0c4fd9ce7c.
```

CI failure attribution before sync:

```text
PR #99124 was merge-conflicting with current origin/main. daily_fix.sh check-main-drift required sync-main for merge conflicts and overlapping related files.
The conflict was in src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.ts and was resolved by combining main's SecretRef discovery short-circuit with this PR's managed-key/source preservation behavior.
```

## Maintainer-ready confidence

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for maintainer review. The reported live macOS LaunchAgent + Telegram behavior is covered by zhangguiping-xydt's proof, current rebased head has focused conflict-resolution continuity, and focused tests/typecheck/static checks pass on the synchronized head.
- **Patch quality notes:** Runtime changes are limited to existing helper/render-policy/start-repair paths. The test-only type escapes construct narrow mocked `GatewayService` and config objects for Vitest boundaries and do not affect runtime code. The empty-object return in `collectExistingEnvironmentFileManagedServiceEnvVars` is the explicit no-preserved-values path for callers that have no existing environment or no managed keys.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Compatibility:** Existing macOS LaunchAgent installs now preserve generated env-file SecretRef values during regeneration when the key is still referenced by current config.
- **Auth-provider/security boundary:** The preserved values are credentials such as Telegram bot tokens. Preservation is limited to generated env-file provenance (`file` / `inline-and-file`) and keys still managed by current config SecretRefs.
- **Precedence:** Existing file-backed values are fallback values. State-dir `.env` and current shell SecretRef values still override them so a stale generated env-file token does not beat fresher sources.
- **Acceptable scope:** The patch stays in the gateway install-plan/render policy and start-repair caller wiring. It does not add Telegram-specific behavior or a new secret store.

## What was not changed

- Telegram channel startup logic.
- SecretRef resolution semantics.
- Non-macOS service rendering behavior.
- Where secrets are stored.
- Ordinary inline stale service env values that do not have generated env-file provenance.
- Unrelated extension behavior; this update only resolves the current main merge conflict in the gateway service-env planning path.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The LaunchAgent reader can parse `~/.openclaw/service-env/<label>.env` and mark entries as `file`, but `buildGatewayInstallPlan` previously only preserved non-managed existing env vars. During regeneration, `writeManagedServiceEnvKeysToEnvironment` removed managed keys and the render policy only re-added state-dir `.env` or current shell SecretRef values. An existing generated env-file Telegram token was therefore lost when the current shell did not contain it.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix restores existing values specifically from `file` / `inline-and-file` provenance for keys still referenced by current config SecretRefs, then lets state-dir `.env` and current shell SecretRef values override them. Start-time repair now forwards the same `environmentValueSources` metadata into that install-plan path.
